newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest spot power eases with limited demand.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest spot power eases with limited demand.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. mostly eased Monday with power demand being limited by milder temperatures, industry sources said.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), Tuesday peak, non-firm power prices were pegged lower at $16.50-18.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from $17.00-20.00 on Friday for Monday delivery, the brokers and marketers said.

MAPP temperatures were forecast to be near normal to five to 10 degrees above normal from Monday through Wednesday, with some cooler weather expected heading into the weekend with calls of zero to five degrees below normal.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP next day power was said to be lower at $11.00-13.00 from $12.00-14.00 on Friday.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Tuesday were assessed at $16.50-17.50 from $19.00-22.00 on Friday, the sources said.
Temperatures in MAIN were expected to be near normal through Thursday, then falling to zero to five degrees below normal heading into the weekend.
MAIN off peak next day power was said to be lower at $11.00-13.00 from $12.00-14.00 on Friday.

In MAIN, Commonwealth Edison's 794 MW Dresden 3 nuclear power unit was producing at near 70 percent of capacity as of early Monday and was increasing power from a maintenance shutdown which began Oct 26.

Also, Commonwealth Edison's 1,105 MW Byron nuclear power unit 2 returned to full power as of Monday morning after cutting power output to 20 percent of capacity last week to repair a pressure switch on a feedwater isolation valve.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Tuesday were said to be discussed lower at 15.00-17.50 from $16.00-18.00 on Friday, the sources said.
Temperatures in ECAR were expected to be slightly above normal through Tuesday then turning cooler, averaging close to normal Wednesday and Thursday.

In ECAR, Consumers Power Co said its 780 megawatt Palisades nuclear power plant in Michigan may resume electricity production on Feb 9 following a shutdown Jan 23 after a problem with electrical equipment at a main generator.
In Tennessee, TVA Nuclear reduced power output at its Browns Ferry 2 nuclear power plant to 29 percent of its 1,065 megawatt (MW) capacity for drain heater maintenance.
Also, TVA Nuclear's 1,170 megawatt (MW) Watts Bar nuclear power unit restarted and was operating at 97 percent of capacity early Monday.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm next day delivery were notionally assessed lower at $12.00-14.00 from $13.00-15.00 per MWh on Friday.
March ECAR was said to be talked at $20.20-20.75, while the final peak three weeks of February were assessed at $21.50-22.00 per MWh.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Tuesday delivery were pegged lower at $13.00-15.00 in the south and $14.50-16.50 in the north from $14.00-16.50 through the entire region on Friday, the sources said.
Off-peak non-firm next day prices throughout SPP were assessed steady at $10.00-12.00 per MWh.
In SPP, temperatures were forecast to be slightly above normal in the west to four to eight degrees above normal in the rest of the region through Tuesday.
March peak SPP was said to be talked in a range of $20.15-20.35 per MWh.
((--Chris Reese, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1627))
